advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a regression test that forces apt-get update to fail and asserts its error tail reaches stderr.
evidence: scripts/install_sandbox_bwrap.sh:23: `apt_quiet "apt-get update" apt-get update -qq` — update is wrapped by the same helper
The fake apt-get always `exit 0` for `update` (test line 25-28); `fail_install` only toggles the install branch
Commit message: 'prints the final apt lines when update or install fails' — update failure is a claimed behavior but untested
The fake apt-get returns exit 0 unconditionally for update: `update) echo "quiet success output that should stay hidden"; exit 0` (tests/scripts/test_install_sandbox_bwrap.py:25-28).
The script adds a distinct update invocation whose failure must surface: `apt_quiet "apt-get update" apt-get update -qq` (scripts/install_sandbox_bwrap.sh:23).

Named violating input: a fake apt-get whose `update` subcommand exits non-zero (e.g. exit 42) — the test suite would not detect if the update failure stopped surfacing the '::error::apt-get update failed' tail (or if `set -euo pipefail` masking regressed the exit propagation).
advisory.finding: The regression tests exercise only the apt-get install failure path; the apt-get update failure path (which the helper also wraps and which the commit message explicitly claims to cover) has no test. A regression that silences update failures would not be caught.
merged_from: The apt-get update failure branch is never exercised; the fake apt-get always exits 0 on 'update', so only the install failure path drives apt_quiet's error branch.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test invoking install_sandbox_bwrap.sh with no arguments, asserting returncode==2 and the usage ::error:: on stderr.
evidence: scripts/install_sandbox_bwrap.sh:4-7 adds `if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then echo "::error::usage: ..." >&2; exit 2; fi`
Both tests always call the script with one package: `["bash", str(SCRIPT), "bubblewrap"]` (tests/scripts/test_install_sandbox_bwrap.py:50). No test invokes it with zero args.

Named violating input: `bash install_sandbox_bwrap.sh` (no packages) — the added guard must exit 2 and emit the usage error; a regression that changed the exit code or dropped the guard would not be caught.
advisory.finding: The added no-argument usage guard (exit 2 with a usage ::error::) is never exercised by any test.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `test_no_args_reports_usage(tmp_path)` running the script with no package args, asserting `result.returncode == 2` and `"usage: install_sandbox_bwrap.sh" in result.stderr`.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider building the install label from "$*" quoted (or drop the label interpolation) to avoid glob/word-split in the diagnostic string.
evidence: Only the label uses $*; the executed command correctly uses "$@", so this affects only the diagnostic text, not the install
dropped.finding: The install label passed to apt_quiet is built with unquoted `$*` (`apt_quiet "apt-get install $*" ...`), so the diagnostic label word-splits and re-globs the package list; a package argument containing a glob metacharacter or IFS whitespace would render a misleading label in the ::error:: line, though the actual install uses the correct "$@".
